key_insight: Prostate MRI at 0.55T can be performed in a PI-RADS-compliant way with image quality and lesion detection that are close to 3T for patient-level assessment.
clinical_relevance: This supports low-field prostate MRI as a potential access-expanding option when high-field scanners are limited, while still aiming for diagnostic-quality imaging.
method: 15 healthy volunteers and 22 patients with suspected prostate cancer underwent bi-parametric prostate MRI at 0.55T.
Protocol included tri-planar T2-weighted imaging and axial diffusion-weighted imaging, with deep learning reconstruction used to improve image quality.
Patient lesion detection at 0.55T was compared against 3T as the reference standard.
evidence_signal: At least acceptable diagnostic quality (PI-QUAL ≥2/3) was achieved in 95% of patients and all controls, with patient-level lesion detection sensitivity of 91% for both readers and no significant difference from 3T.
watch_item: Results are from a small single-study cohort, so broader generalizability and real-world workflow performance still need confirmation.
paper_title: Feasibility of PI-RADS Compliant Prostate MRI at 0.55T
